headline: Congress canceled an EPA rule that kept certain stricter pollution controls on facilities that reclassify to a lower-emitting category under the Clean Air Act.
what_it_does: This resolution uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel an EPA rule. The rule said that facilities releasing certain long-lasting, build-up-in-the-body hazardous air pollutants had to keep using some of their major-source pollution controls if they reclassified as smaller "area sources." With the rule canceled, those facilities no longer have to meet those major-source requirements after reclassifying. Area sources generally face less strict standards.

who_it_affects.group: Industrial facilities that emit persistent and bioaccumulative hazardous air pollutants
who_it_affects.how: If they reclassify from major sources to area sources, they are no longer required by this rule to keep their major-source emission controls.
The agency's rule is voided, and under the Congressional Review Act it generally cannot issue a substantially similar rule without new authority from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: People who live near facilities that reclassify as area sources
who_it_affects.how: The pollution standards that apply to nearby facilities that reclassify may be less strict than under the canceled rule.

when_it_takes_effect: June 20, 2025, when the resolution was signed into law.
